lines: Shifts a 1V/octave signal up or down by musical intervals picked with toggles, adding the chosen intervals together and sliding between totals when they change
Chooses whether the chosen intervals are added to the input or taken away from it, the green up lamp showing addition and the red dn lamp subtraction
Adds one semitone to the shift while it is on
Adds two semitones to the shift while it is on
Adds three semitones to the shift while it is on
Adds four semitones to the shift while it is on
Adds seven semitones to the shift while it is on
Adds twelve semitones to the shift while it is on
Sets how long the output takes to slide to a new total, 10ms fully counter-clockwise and 100ms fully clockwise
A gate above 2V forces the intervals to be added rather than taken away, whatever the up and dn toggle is set to
A gate above 2V adds a further semitone to the shift, on top of the toggle beside it
A gate above 2V adds a further two semitones to the shift, on top of the toggle beside it
A gate above 2V adds a further three semitones to the shift, on top of the toggle beside it
A gate above 2V adds a further four semitones to the shift, on top of the toggle beside it
A gate above 2V adds a further seven semitones to the shift, on top of the toggle beside it
A gate above 2V adds a further twelve semitones to the shift, on top of the toggle beside it
The 1V/octave signal to be shifted, and its channel count sets the channel count of the output
The input with the whole shift applied, sliding into place at the rate set by gliss
Note — the two-digit display counts the total shift in semitones.
HarMoNee.notes: The module carries a second output, named Echo of Input, which has no jack on the panel and so is untagged.

lines: Slews a changing control voltage over a fixed time rather than a fixed slope, so every move takes the same length of time whatever its size
Sets how long a move takes, 0 to 1 second, with a floor of ten samples
The changing voltage to be slewed, and its channel count sets the channel count of both outputs
Lengthens the glide by a fifth of a second per volt and shortens it by the same on negative voltage, over the slider setting
The input sliding toward each new value over the glide time
10V on a channel while that channel is sliding and 0V once it has arrived, despite the maker's tooltip calling it a gate at the end of the gliss
Note — a new target part way through a move turns the slide around from where it has reached rather than jumping to it.
Glissinator.notes: The maker's tooltip calls the gate output a gate at the end of the gliss; the installed code and the README both make it high for the whole of the slide and low once it finishes.

lines: Polyrhythmic clock generator running a base clock and five more clocks at whole-number fractions of it, each with a gate and a tempo CV output
Sets the base tempo, 30 to 480 beats per minute, with 120 at noon
Starts and stops every clock
Returns every clock to the start of its cycle while it is pressed
Sets how many base beats pass between automatic resets, 0 to 64, with no automatic reset at 0
Sets how many beats that clock fits into the base-beat count set by its per M base knob, 1 to 32
Sets how many base beats that clock's beat count is spread over, 1 to 32
Sets the fraction of each of that clock's cycles for which its gate is high, a square gate at 0.5
A trigger here switches between running and stopped
A trigger here returns every clock to the start of its cycle
Sets the base tempo in place of the BPM knob, 0V giving 120 beats per minute and a volt for each doubling
A 10V gate at the base tempo, high for half of each beat
A 10V gate at the rate of that clock, high for the fraction of each cycle set by its p/w knob
The base tempo as a voltage, 0V at 120 beats per minute and a volt for each doubling
That clock's tempo as a voltage, 0V at 120 beats per minute and a volt for each doubling
A 10V trigger 96 samples long each time running starts or stops
A 10V trigger 96 samples long each time a reset happens
Quantizer clamping a 1V/octave signal to twelfths of a volt, with each of the twelve notes switched in or out of the scale
Shifts the whole scale in twelfths of a volt, 0 to 12, so that the R note falls somewhere other than a whole volt
Switches that note in and out of the scale; an input landing on a note that is switched out is quantized down to the nearest note left switched in
The 1V/octave signal to be quantized, and its channel count sets the channel count of both outputs
The quantized 1V/octave signal
A 10V trigger lasting 15ms each time the quantized note changes
Menu — Major, Natural Minor, Harmonic Minor and Whole Tone set the twelve note switches to that scale, rooted on R.
Developer tool that runs a check over whichever module it is patched to and prints the warnings and the findings on its screen; it makes no sound
Patching a cable from here to an output on another module makes that module the one checked
Patching a cable from here to an input on another module makes that module the one checked
Note — the test button picks which check runs: Labels Check, Probe Bypass, JSON Extract, WidgetPositions, WhiteList or MyPatch.
Note — Output To writes the current report to standard output, to an HTML file opened in a browser, or to the Rack log.
Sends each clock tick at random to an A side or a B side and holds a fresh random voltage for whichever side was picked
Sets how many channels the outputs carry, 1 to 16, each drawing its own random numbers
Sets the balance between the two sides, every tick going to A fully clockwise, every tick going to B fully counter-clockwise, and an even split at noon, the other way round from the maker's tooltip
Sets the span of the random voltages, 0 to 10V
Adds an offset of -5V to 5V to every random voltage, setting the bottom of the random range rather than its middle, despite the maker's Center label
In latch a side's gate stays high until the other side is picked and its voltage holds until then; in passthrough the clock passes through and a new voltage is drawn every tick
A rising edge picks a side for each channel and draws new random voltages
Shifts the balance between the two sides, 5V sending every tick to A and -5V sending every tick to B
Carries a gate on each channel whose most recent tick went to A, 10V in latch and the incoming clock voltage in passthrough
The random voltage held for the A side, scaled and offset by the Rand CV knobs
Carries a gate on each channel whose most recent tick went to B, 10V in latch and the incoming clock voltage in passthrough
The random voltage held for the B side, scaled and offset by the Rand CV knobs
An echo of the incoming clock on every channel
A new random voltage drawn on every tick whichever side was picked, scaled and offset by the Rand CV knobs
LuckyHold.notes: The maker's tooltip for the chance knob reads 'A (-1) or B (1) chance?', but the installed code sends every tick to B at -1 and every tick to A at 1; the lines follow the code. The centre knob is added to a random value that runs from zero upward, so it sets the bottom of the range rather than its middle.

lines: Sets the contrast of Rack's own menus and tooltips; it has no jacks and makes no sound
Menu — Default, High Contrast Light and High Contrast Dark set the colours Rack draws its menus and tooltips in, and the choice is saved with the patch.
Shows the file name of the open patch, with the folder holding it in smaller lettering; it has no jacks and makes no sound
Delays a signal by a whole number of samples, on each of up to 16 polyphonic channels
Sets the delay: the input passes straight through at 1 and each step up adds one sample, to 98 samples at 99
The signal to be delayed, and its channel count sets the channel count of the output
The input delayed by the amount set by the # samples knob
Recreation of the NES noise generator, with that chip's long and short pseudo-random sequences and no envelope
Picks one of the sixteen NES noise periods, 0 to 15, the noise growing coarser and lower as the number rises
Chooses between the long pseudo-random sequence and the short repeating ones
Chooses which short sequence runs, 93 bits long or 31 bits long, and does nothing while the long sequence is chosen
Picks which of the 352 distinct 93-bit sequences runs, 0 to 351, and does nothing unless the short 93-bit sequence is chosen
Sets the noise period in place of the knob, 0V to 10V covering all sixteen of them
The noise, -5V to 5V
Recreation of the two tonal oscillators of the NES, a pulse wave with four duty cycles and a fixed 32-step triangle
Sets the pitch in semitones, 54 either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Picks the duty cycle of the pulse wave: 0 for an eighth, 1 for a quarter, 2 for a half and 3 for three quarters
Raises the pitch of both waves by an octave per volt
The pulse wave, -5V to 5V
The NES triangle wave, -5V to 5V, stepping through 32 levels
Oscillator running the NES triangle-wave engine over a 32-step waveform drawn by hand rather than the chip's fixed ramp
Sets the pitch in semitones, 54 either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets the level of that step of the 32-step waveform, 0 to 15, with the zero crossing between 7 and 8; click or drag on the column to set it
Raises the pitch by an octave per volt, and its channel count sets the channel count of the output
The drawn waveform, -5V to 5V
Note — the output carries as many channels as the v/o input, so nothing sounds while that jack is empty.
ChipYourWave.notes: The module declares 32 further inputs, one per waveform step, which have no jacks on the panel and are untagged. It is hidden in the module browser.

lines: Wrapper around Robin Schmidt's open303, a monophonic 303-style bass voice with a built-in acid sequencer pattern
Blends the oscillator from a saw at 0 to a square at 1
Sets the tuning reference, 400Hz to 480Hz, with A at 440Hz by default
Sets the filter cutoff, held at 261.63Hz over the lower half of the travel and climbing ten octaves above that over the upper half
Sets the filter resonance, 0 to 100 percent
Sets how much of the envelope is applied to the filter cutoff, 0 to 100 percent
Sets the decay time of the filter envelope, 200ms to 2 seconds
Sets how much louder and brighter an accented step is than an unaccented one, 0 to 100 percent
Sets the output level, -60dB to 0dB
Picks the mode of the 303 filter model
Runs the built-in acid sequencer pattern in place of notes arriving at the gate input
Sets the pitch of the note, 0V giving middle C, read at the moment the gate opens
A rising edge starts a note, which ends when the voltage falls below 0.5V
Sets how hard the note is struck, 0V to 10V covering the MIDI velocity range, with 100 used while the jack is empty
Shifts the saw-to-square blend, a tenth of a volt covering the whole of it
Raises the tuning reference by 3Hz per volt
Raises the filter cutoff by an octave per volt
Raises the resonance by 10 percent per volt
Raises the envelope amount by 10 percent per volt
Lengthens the filter envelope decay by 400ms per volt
Raises the accent amount by 10 percent per volt
Raises the output level by a thirtieth of a decibel per volt
The voice, one channel however many channels arrive at the gate input
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the filter model is picked by the knob above it alone
Open303.notes: Hidden in the module browser and described by the maker as alpha. The CV jack under filttype is never read by the installed code, so it has no line. Five further parameters exist in the module - amp sustain and three high-pass corners and a square phase shift - with no control on the panel.

lines: Polyphonic plucked-string voice built on the Karplus-Strong algorithm, each pluck ringing on and fading out by itself
Plucks a string on the first channel each time it is pressed
A rising edge plucks a string on that channel, which takes the pitch and the other settings as they stand at that moment
Sets the pitch of a pluck in semitones, 54 either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Raises the pitch of a pluck by an octave per volt
Picks the burst the string is filled with at the pluck: random, square, saw, noisysaw, sin or sinchirp
Picks the starting burst in place of the knob, 0V to 10V running through the six of them
Sets the weight of the one-sample averaging filter that damps the string, 0 to 1, damping hardest in the middle of that range
Shifts the filter weight by a tenth per volt
Sets how fast a pluck dies away, a long ring at 0.1 and a short one at 4
Shortens the ring, adding one to the decay setting per volt
Fades every sounding string out quickly
The sounding strings, -2V to 2V, on one polyphonic channel per triggered channel
Changes the filter name shown on the display and nothing else; one string filter is built into the module and every pluck uses it
Nothing in the module reads this control; only the A weight is fed to the one string filter that is built
Note — thirty-two voices are shared out over the channels, so two plucks close together on one channel both ring.
KarplusStrongPoly.notes: Only one string filter is built, so the Filter knob and the jack beside it change the reading on the display and nothing else, and the B and C knobs and their jacks are read by nothing; none of them has a line. The A knob and the atten knob are never given a range by the maker's code, so their tooltips show no name.

lines: Ring modulator built on a model of a diode ring, multiplying a signal by a carrier
Blends between the untouched signal fully counter-clockwise and the ring-modulated signal fully clockwise
The signal to be modulated, and its channel count sets the channel count of the output
The carrier the signal is multiplied by
The blend of modulated and untouched signal
Distortion built from a coarse level quantizer and a clipping amplifier, either of which can be switched out of the path
Blends between the untouched input fully counter-clockwise and the processed signal fully clockwise
Shifts the blend toward the processed signal by a tenth of the way per volt
Switches the level quantizer in and out of the signal path
Sets how many levels the signal is quantized to, 2 for the coarsest and 16 for the smoothest
Raises the number of levels the signal is quantized to, a volt adding about three steps of the knob's scale
Switches the clipping amplifier in and out of the signal path
Sets the gain fed into the clipper, one at the counter-clockwise end and eleven at the clockwise end
Raises the gain fed into the clipper by one per volt
The signal to be distorted, and its channel count sets the channel count of the output
The distorted signal, clipped at -5V to 5V whenever the clipping amplifier is switched in
Generates polyphonic test signals, pitch and velocity and gate, from nine built-in patterns, four of them played from MIDI files
Sets the tempo, 15 to 480 beats per minute, with 120 at the default setting
Sets how many polyphonic channels are generated, 1 to 16, raised where the chosen pattern needs more
Picks the pattern: RND TUNE, ARPS, CIRC O 5, RND CHRD, CHAOS, GOLDBERG, LV BEETH, CHOPIN or DEBUSSY
Sets the one extra control a pattern offers, density for CHAOS and which piece is played for the MIDI patterns, with the lamp lit while the chosen pattern reads it
The pitch of each generated note in volts per octave
The velocity of each generated note, 0V to 10V
A 10V gate for as long as each generated note sounds
The maker's own scratchpad for trying out panel widgets, hidden in the module browser
A voltage above 2V here unhides the module in the browser, and it is hidden again when the voltage falls
Nothing in the module reads or drives this control; it is on the panel only to lay out a widget
BaconTest.notes: Every other knob and jack is there to lay out a widget and is read by nothing, so none of them has a line.

lines: Shuts Rack down on a trigger, with nothing else on the panel
A rising edge here closes Rack; the jack is ignored for the first 12000 samples after the module loads
